# Arrow navigation leaves a suspended grid edit unresolved

## Context

Leaf of #18762. The GPT return evaluation reproduced a missing part of [D17832 OQ2 / criterion 5](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/17832): an arrow while the editor is suspended is an explicit leave-edit intent. A valid draft commits before navigation; an invalid draft blocks navigation and reprojects.

Measured in headed Chromium 153 at `dev@ab2e7cd17c4279cc8d5cb36b2ecd119f06f00a60`, on the existing `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-cell-editing` fixture, both its stock 40-column/400-row shape and a 120-column scale variant. No page or console errors in the confirming runs.

## The Problem

Click record 3's `c3`, press Enter, type `arrow-draft`, then set the pooled View's vertical scroll to 5000 so the editor unmounts. Press ArrowDown while the View holds focus.

| Case | Observed | Required |
|---|---|---|
| valid `c3` draft | selection moves record 3 → 4; record 3 still holds `r3c3`; its edit session survives | commit the draft, end that session, then navigate |
| required `c5` cleared to an invalid draft | selection still moves 3 → 4; editor reappears incidentally as the row comes back, without focus | keep selection, reproject/focus the invalid editor and announce validation |
| Tab controls, same states | valid commits and edits the adjacent cell; invalid reprojects, keeps selection and focuses its editor | already correct |

Keyboard activation avoids the known double-click selection-toggle confound. Reads follow rendered selection and an App-Worker round trip, not a same-tick focus guess.

## The Architectural Reality

- `CellEditing#getViewKeys` owns Enter, Escape, F2 and Tab; its `onTabKey` already owns commit-if-valid and invalid-session reprojection.
- `selection.grid.CellModel` and `RowModel` consume arrows. Their shared `BaseModel#hasEditorFocus` checks the event's physical editor path; a suspended editor has no such path.
- `util.KeyNavigation#onKeyDown` invokes every matching registration; appending another arrow handler would not establish ordering or veto the selection handler.
- `CellEditing#onSelectionChange` retires owed refocus; it does not resolve the edit terminal.

## The Fix

Add a shared navigation admission step before the existing selection models move. Keep edit validation, commitment and invalid-session reprojection in CellEditing. The mounted editor/picker retains its own key handling; with no suspended edit, navigation is unchanged.

Reuse the plugin's invalid-Tab reveal/focus behavior rather than copy field validation into each selection model. Extend the existing grid editing tests and document the suspended-arrow rule.

Prescription checked: `src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs` owns edit terminals; `src/selection/grid/BaseModel.mjs` owns the shared selection-side gate. `CellModel.mjs` and `RowModel.mjs` are the existing arrow consumers. No new module or subsystem is prescribed. Structure map: N/A — Engine behavior, existing owners.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Edge case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| View arrows during a suspended edit | D17832 OQ2 / criterion 5 | resolve a valid edit before existing model navigation | invalid blocks navigation and restores editor focus; no session stays unchanged | plugin/gate JSDoc; Grids guide | real-key, worker-state e2e controls |
| Mounted editor keys | existing `BaseModel#hasEditorFocus` and field key handlers | editor retains its keys | picker and number-field controls stay valid | preserve current docs | existing field/grid coverage plus focused control |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For a valid edit suspended by vertical or horizontal pooling, each applicable arrow direction commits exactly once, destroys the old editor/session, then uses the selection model's existing navigation.
- [ ] For an invalid suspended draft, the arrow changes neither record nor logical selection; its cell is brought into sight and the same editor receives focus with validation visible.
- [ ] Both cell- and row-selecting models obey the terminal; derived row/column combinations keep their normal navigation semantics.
- [ ] Mounted input/picker keys, no-edit navigation, neutral scrolling and suspended Tab/Shift+Tab remain unchanged.
- [ ] CI-executed real-key coverage is red before the fix and mutation-sensitive to omission of the terminal or invalid-draft veto; the guide states the delivered behavior.

## Out of Scope

Pointer/focus-leave policy while suspended; RowModel activation and post-edit anchoring (#18941); column-highlight synchronization (#18950); fixture geometry (#18951); a general key-dispatch rewrite.

## Avoided Traps

- Adding a competing View arrow listener and depending on registration order.
- Committing on every `selectionChange`: that occurs after the mutation and conflates pointer, programmatic and keyboard changes.
- Raising a timer or waiting for `containsFocus`; the logical session and event target already name the state.

Decision Record: NOT_NEEDED, preserved from D17832. Decision Record impact: none.
